;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The [[Yemeni Army]] says that scores of [[Houthi]] [[militia]]men were killed in clashes and that scores of others were wounded in the central [[Al Bayda Governorate]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/yemeni-army-houthis-clash-in-central-province/1841516 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**The [[Taliban]] [[ambush]] a group of [[Afghan Army|soldiers]] in [[Khan Abad District|Khan Abad]], [[Kunduz Province|Kunduz]], killing three of them. Five Taliban [[insurgent]]s are killed in the clash. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/3-police-5-taliban-killed-kunduz-clashes (Tolo News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[Economy of the United States]]
***The [[United States House of Representatives|United States House]] passes a $3 trillion coronavirus relief package. The bill will head to the [[United States Senate]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-vote-democrats-3t-coronavirus-heroes-aid-stimulus-checks-money-n1207816 (NBC News)] 
*[[Coronavirus recession]] 
**American retail chain [[J. C. Penney]] files for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] after accumulating $4.2 billion in debt. It will also close an unspecified number of stores. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2020/05/15/jc-penney-bankruptcy-store-closings-coronavirus-closures-chapter-11/3057838001/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Indonesia]] announces that it is imposing a [[value added tax]] on the digital services provided by [[internet]] companies. The tax will take effect in July. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indonesia-tax-digital/indonesia-to-impose-vat-on-streaming-other-digital-services-from-july-idUSKBN22R23V (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[United States Air Force]] [[Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor|F-22 Raptor]] [[Stealth aircraft|stealth fighter]] crashes outside of [[Eglin Air Force Base]], [[Florida]], the pilot safely [[Ejection seat|ejects]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/f-22-stealth-fighter-crashes-near-eglin-air-force-base-2020-5 (''Business Insider'')]
*An earthquake with a magnitude of 6.5 strikes near [[Tonopah, Nevada]], with several [[aftershock]]s reported, though no injuries are reported. The earthquake is the largest in the state since 1954. [https://www.rgj.com/story/news/2020/05/15/magnitude-6-4-earthquake-has-struck-near-tonopah/5196927002/ (''Reno Gazette-Journal'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
****[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] extends the stay-at-home order for [[New York (state)|New York]] until June 13. [https://www.businessinsider.com/new-york-governor-cuomo-stay-at-home-order-june-13-2020-5 (''Business Insider'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] passes 50,000 cases of COVID-19, the seventh state in the U.S. to do so. As of this date, this state has 50,079 reported cases, causing 4,825 deaths. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/05/michigan-surpasses-50k-confirmed-cases-of-coronavirus.html (MLive.com)]
***[[President of the United States|United States President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces the officials for [[Operation Warp Speed]] in an effort to develop a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] by the end of 2020. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/05/15/trump-coronavirus-vaccine-development-team-260678 (''Politico'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
***The [[Roads and Transport Authority (Dubai)|Dubai Road Transport Authority]] announces that the elevators on the [[Dubai Metro]] will be restricted to two people at a time. [https://gulfnews.com/uae/coronavirus-new-rule-at-dubai-metro---only-2-people-can-use-elevator-at-a-time-1.71515526 (''Gulf News'')]
**The death toll from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] exceeds 300,000 worldwide. [https://www.timesnownews.com/india/article/global-covid-19-death-toll-crosses-300000-mark-us-leads-the-world-in-confirmed-cases/592123 (TimesnowNews)]

;International relations
*[[Afghanistan–United States relations]], [[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**[[Vice President of Afghanistan]] [[Amrullah Saleh]] rejects U.S. assertion that [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] are responsible for the attack on the maternity hospital this week and instead blames the [[Taliban]]. The Taliban previously denied the accusation and labeled the attack as "heinous". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks/afghans-say-taliban-behind-bloodshed-reject-u-s-blame-of-islamic-state-idUSKBN22R1QJ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
**[[Colombia]]n Ministers of [[Ministry of National Defense (Colombia)|Defense]], [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Colombia)|Foreign Affairs]] and [[Ministry of Health and Social Protection (Colombia)|Health]] meet with their [[Brazil]]ian counterparts to coordinate a joint response to the increasing numbers of COVID-19 cases in [[Brazil–Colombia border|the border region]] between both countries. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-colombia-brazil-idUSKBN22S023?taid=5ebf560e691abf0001ee87fb&utm_campaign=trueAnthem%3A+Trending+Content&utm_medium=trueAnthem&utm_source=twitter (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Georgian President]] [[Salome Zourabichvili]] pardons two opposition politicians in a move to reduce political tension ahead of a parliamentary election. The pardoned are the former [[mayor of Tbilisi]] [[Gigi Ugulava]] and ex-defense minister [[Irakli Okruashvili]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-georgia-president-pardon/georgian-president-pardons-two-opposition-politicians-idUSKBN22R2XA (Reuters)]
*[[Ghana Police Service|Ghanaian police]] names ''[[Coronation Street]]'' actor [[Philip Middlemiss]] as one of the four suspects in a [[Pound Sterling|£]]5 million [[bribery]] scandal over the sale of [[military aircraft|military plane]]s, and asks he be turned over for questioning. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/coronation-st-actor-philip-middlemiss-wanted-over-sale-of-military-planes-to-ghana-p0bjntjnh (''The Times'')]
*[[Germany]]'s [[Bundestag]] votes to make the [[flag-burning|burning]] of the [[Flag of Europe|EU flag]] or that of another country a [[hate crime]] equivalent to that of burning the [[German flag]] - carrying a sentence of up to three years in prison. The only major party that opposed the move was the [[Alternative for Germany]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/amp/world-europe-52674809 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections

**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Nelson Teich]] resigns as [[Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Minister of Health]] less than a month into office amid disagreements with [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] over the federal government's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-52682358 (BBC News)]
**[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]]
***[[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] announces the [[2020 New Jersey Democratic primary|New Jersey primary]] will primarily be conducted via vote-by-mail. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-jersey-governor-announces-july-primary-will-be-vote-by-mail/ (CBS News)]
